chapters.title: Hannah prays and dedicates Samuel

parts.text: Elkanah’s wife Hannah is childless, while Peninnah has children and provokes her bitterly. During the family’s yearly visit to Shiloh, Hannah prays in distress and vows that, if God gives her a son, she will give him to the LORD throughout his life. Eli mistakes her silent prayer for drunkenness, but accepts her explanation and sends her away with a blessing. She eats and is no longer sad.

The LORD remembers Hannah, and she bears Samuel. After weaning him, she brings him to the LORD’s house with offerings. She reminds Eli that she is the woman who prayed there and declares that God has granted her request. She gives Samuel to the LORD for all his days, and worship is offered there.

chapters.title: Hannah’s praise and Eli’s corrupt household

parts.text: Hannah praises the LORD’s holiness, knowledge, and power to reverse human fortunes: he humbles the strong, raises the poor, gives life, and guards his saints. Samuel ministers before Eli, but Eli’s sons abuse their priestly office by seizing sacrificial portions and treating offerings with contempt. Hannah brings Samuel a little coat each year, and God gives her more children.

Eli rebukes his sons for their evil conduct, including sexual wrongdoing, but they refuse to listen. Samuel continues growing in favour with God and people. A man of God announces judgment on Eli’s house for honouring his sons above the LORD. Both sons will die on one day, and God will raise a faithful priest while Eli’s descendants suffer loss and dependence.

chapters.title: The LORD calls Samuel

parts.text: While Samuel serves under Eli, the LORD’s word is rare and open visions are uncommon. Samuel hears his name called at night and repeatedly goes to Eli, thinking he summoned him. Eli eventually recognizes that the LORD is calling the boy and tells him how to answer. When the call comes again, Samuel presents himself as God’s listening servant.

God announces irreversible judgment against Eli’s house because Eli knew his sons’ wickedness and failed to restrain them. Samuel fears telling him, but Eli insists on hearing everything and submits to the LORD’s decision. As Samuel grows, God is with him and lets none of his words fall to the ground. All Israel recognizes him as an established prophet, and the LORD continues revealing himself at Shiloh.

chapters.title: The ark is captured and Eli dies

parts.text: Israel is defeated by the Philistines and brings the ark from Shiloh into battle, expecting it to save them. Hophni and Phinehas accompany it. The Philistines fear the news but resolve to fight, and Israel suffers a far greater defeat. The ark is captured, and Eli’s two sons are killed, fulfilling the announced sign against his house.

A messenger reaches Shiloh, where the aged, blind Eli waits anxiously. On hearing that the ark has been taken, he falls backward, breaks his neck, and dies after forty years of judging Israel. Phinehas’ pregnant wife goes into labour at the news and dies after giving birth. She names the child I-chabod, lamenting that glory has departed because the ark of God is captured.

chapters.title: The ark brings judgment in Philistine cities

parts.text: The Philistines place the captured ark beside Dagon in Ashdod’s temple. The next morning Dagon lies facedown before it. After they restore the image, it falls again with its head and hands broken off upon the threshold. Thereafter, Dagon’s priests and worshippers avoid treading on that threshold.

The LORD’s hand strikes Ashdod and its territory with painful disease, and the people demand removal of the ark. It is sent to Gath, where another outbreak causes panic, then toward Ekron, whose people fear destruction. The Philistine rulers gather and resolve to send it back to its place. Death and suffering spread, and the city’s cry rises to heaven.

chapters.title: The ark returns to Israel

parts.text: After seven months, the Philistines ask their priests and diviners how to return the ark. They advise a trespass offering of golden emerods and mice and warn against hardening their hearts like Egypt. The ark and gifts are placed on a new cart drawn by two milch kine separated from their calves. If the kine go toward Beth-shemesh, the Philistines will recognize the LORD’s hand in their suffering. They do so directly.

The people of Beth-shemesh rejoice, and sacrifices are offered using the cart’s wood and the kine. Philistine rulers watch and return home. The LORD later strikes men of Beth-shemesh for looking into the ark. Alarmed, the people ask who can stand before this holy God and invite Kirjath-jearim to receive it.

chapters.title: Repentance, victory, and Samuel’s judgeship

parts.text: The ark is placed in Abinadab’s house at Kirjath-jearim, with Eleazar appointed to guard it. After a long period, Israel laments after the LORD. Samuel calls them to remove foreign gods and serve him alone. They obey, gather at Mizpeh, fast, and confess sin. When the Philistines attack, Samuel sacrifices and cries to God, who thunders against the enemy and throws them into confusion. Israel pursues and defeats them.

Samuel sets up a stone named Eben-ezer, declaring that the LORD has helped them thus far. Philistine power is checked, captured cities are restored, and peace holds with the Amorites. Samuel judges Israel throughout his life, travelling a yearly circuit through Beth-el, Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and returning to Ramah, where he builds an altar to the LORD.

chapters.title: Israel demands a king

parts.text: When Samuel grows old, his sons serve as judges but accept bribes and pervert justice. Israel’s elders ask for a king like other nations. Samuel is displeased and prays. The LORD tells him that the people’s rejection is ultimately of God’s kingship, consistent with their earlier forsaking of him. Samuel must hear their request but warn them clearly about royal rule.

Samuel describes how a king will take sons for war and labour, daughters for service, the best land, servants, animals, and a tenth of produce and flocks. The people will eventually cry out under the burden. Nevertheless, they insist on a king to judge them and fight their battles. God directs Samuel to grant their request.

chapters.title: Saul meets Samuel

parts.text: Saul, the tall and notable son of Kish, searches with a servant for his father’s missing asses. After an unsuccessful journey, Saul considers returning, but the servant suggests consulting a man of God in the nearby city. They arrange a small gift and seek the seer, meeting Samuel as he is going to a sacrifice.

The LORD has already told Samuel that a Benjamite will come and that he is to be anointed captain to deliver Israel from the Philistines. Samuel assures Saul that the asses are found and hints at the honour awaiting him. Saul protests his family’s insignificance. At the feast he receives a place of honour and a reserved portion. The next morning Samuel sends the servant ahead so he can privately declare God’s word to Saul.

chapters.title: Saul is anointed and publicly chosen

parts.text: Samuel anoints Saul and gives confirming signs involving news of the asses, travellers with provisions, and a company of prophets. He tells Saul the Spirit will come upon him and directs him to wait at Gilgal for further instructions. The signs occur, God gives Saul another heart, and he prophesies, surprising those who know him. He does not tell his uncle about the kingdom.

Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpeh and reminds them that their demand rejects the God who delivered them. Selection by lot identifies Saul, who is found hiding among the baggage. His height impresses the people, and they acclaim him king. Samuel records the manner of the kingdom. Some men accompany Saul, while others despise him; he holds his peace.

chapters.title: Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead

parts.text: Nahash besieges Jabesh-gilead and offers peace only if every man submits to losing his right eye, bringing shame upon Israel. The city sends messengers for help. When Saul hears, the Spirit of God comes upon him, and he summons Israel by sending pieces of oxen as a warning. A large force gathers, and Saul divides it into three companies, attacks at morning, and thoroughly defeats the Ammonites.

The people now demand punishment for those who questioned Saul’s rule, but he refuses executions on a day when the LORD has delivered Israel. Samuel calls the people to Gilgal to renew the kingdom. There they publicly confirm Saul before the LORD, offer peace offerings, and rejoice greatly.

chapters.title: Samuel warns king and people to obey

parts.text: Samuel publicly asks whether he has defrauded, oppressed, or taken bribes from anyone. Israel declares him innocent. He recounts God’s deliverances and the people’s recurring disobedience, showing that their request for a king arose despite the LORD’s kingship. Now both the people and their king must fear, serve, and obey God; rebellion will bring his hand against them.

At Samuel’s prayer, the LORD sends thunder and rain during wheat harvest as a sign of their wickedness in asking for a king. Frightened, the people request intercession. Samuel urges them not to turn aside but to serve God wholeheartedly, assuring them that the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name. He promises continued prayer and instruction, while warning that persistent evil will consume both them and their king.

chapters.title: Saul offers sacrifice and loses the promise of a dynasty

parts.text: Jonathan attacks a Philistine garrison, provoking a large enemy gathering. Israelites hide or flee, while Saul’s remaining men tremble. After waiting seven days at Gilgal, Saul sees his people scattering and offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives and rebukes him for disobedience. Saul’s kingdom will not continue; the LORD has sought a man after his own heart to command his people.

Samuel leaves, and Saul’s force numbers about six hundred. Philistine raiding parties spread through the land. The chapter explains Israel’s shortage of weapons: the Philistines have prevented them from maintaining smiths, forcing dependence for sharpening tools. Only Saul and Jonathan among the men with them possess sword or spear. A Philistine garrison advances toward the passage of Michmash.

chapters.title: Jonathan’s victory and Saul’s rash oath

parts.text: Jonathan and his armourbearer approach a Philistine outpost, trusting that the LORD can save by many or few. Taking the enemy’s challenge as their sign, they climb up and strike the garrison. Panic spreads, the ground trembles, and the Philistines turn on one another. Saul’s men join the battle, along with Israelites who had hidden or been among the enemy. The LORD saves Israel.

Saul’s oath forbidding food weakens the army, and Jonathan unknowingly eats honey. Hungry soldiers later eat meat with blood, requiring correction. When God does not answer Saul’s inquiry, the lot identifies Jonathan, but the people rescue him from Saul’s death sentence because God worked through him. The chapter closes with Saul’s military achievements, family, officers, and continuing recruitment against the Philistines.

chapters.title: Saul spares Agag and is rejected

parts.text: Samuel commands Saul to destroy Amalek and its possessions because of its earlier attack on Israel. Saul defeats the Amalekites but spares King Agag and the best livestock, destroying what is worthless. God tells Samuel that Saul has turned back from following him. Saul claims obedience when Samuel arrives, but the sound of sheep and oxen exposes the failure. He blames the people and says the animals were kept for sacrifice.

Samuel declares that obedience is better than sacrifice and that rebellion and stubbornness are grave sins. Because Saul rejected God’s word, God rejects him as king. Saul confesses but seeks public honour. Samuel announces the kingdom’s transfer to a better neighbour and executes Agag. The two men separate, and Samuel mourns for Saul.

chapters.title: David is anointed and serves Saul

parts.text: The LORD sends Samuel to Jesse’s household in Beth-lehem to anoint a new king. Samuel initially judges by appearance, but God tells him that he looks on the heart. Jesse’s older sons are passed over. David, the youngest, is brought from tending sheep, and God identifies him as the chosen one. Samuel anoints him, and the Spirit of the LORD comes upon him from that day.

The Spirit of the LORD departs from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubles him. His servants recommend a skilled harp player and identify David. Saul sends for him, loves him greatly, and makes him his armourbearer. Whenever the troubling spirit comes, David plays the harp, Saul finds relief, and the evil spirit departs.

chapters.title: David defeats Goliath

parts.text: The Philistine champion Goliath repeatedly challenges Israel to single combat, and Saul’s army is afraid. Jesse sends David with food for his brothers, and David hears the challenge. He asks about the reward for defeating the man who defies the living God’s armies. His eldest brother rebukes him, but David continues speaking, and his words reach Saul.

David offers to fight, recalling the LORD’s deliverance from a lion and a bear. He declines Saul’s untested armour and takes his staff, sling, and five stones. Goliath mocks him, but David declares that the battle belongs to the LORD. A sling stone strikes Goliath’s forehead; David kills him and cuts off his head with Goliath’s sword. Israel pursues the fleeing Philistines, and Saul asks whose son David is.

chapters.title: Saul grows jealous of David

parts.text: Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him, giving him his robe and weapons. David succeeds in Saul’s service and wins public approval. When women celebrate Saul’s thousands and David’s ten thousands, Saul grows jealous. He twice throws a javelin at David, but David escapes. Saul makes him a military captain, and David’s wise conduct and the LORD’s presence increase both his popularity and Saul’s fear.

Saul offers marriage alliances while hoping Philistine fighting will kill David. Merab is given elsewhere, but Michal loves David. Saul demands a hundred Philistine foreskins as the bride price; David brings two hundred and marries Michal. Recognizing that God is with David and his own daughter loves him, Saul becomes his continuing enemy.

chapters.title: David escapes Saul’s repeated attempts to kill him

parts.text: Saul tells Jonathan and his servants to kill David. Jonathan warns David and argues that he has faithfully served the king and brought Israel great deliverance. Saul swears not to kill him, and David returns. But after another military success, Saul again tries to pin David to the wall with a javelin while he plays the harp. David escapes.

Saul sends men to watch David’s house and kill him in the morning. Michal lowers him through a window and uses an image in the bed to delay discovery. David flees to Samuel at Ramah. Successive groups sent to capture him are overcome by the Spirit and prophesy. Saul himself follows and also prophesies, stripping off his clothes and lying naked before Samuel.

chapters.title: Jonathan confirms Saul’s murderous purpose

parts.text: David asks Jonathan why Saul seeks his life. They arrange a test during the new-moon meal: David will be absent, and Jonathan will observe Saul’s response. They renew their covenant, including lasting kindness toward Jonathan’s household. An agreed signal involving arrows will tell David whether he can safely return or must flee.

When Saul notices David’s absence, Jonathan offers the agreed explanation. Saul erupts in anger, declares David a threat to Jonathan’s kingdom, and throws a javelin at his own son. Jonathan leaves grieving, then goes to the field and gives the warning signal. After dismissing his servant, he and David meet, weep, and reaffirm their covenant before the LORD. David departs while Jonathan returns to the city.

chapters.title: David receives sacred bread and flees to Gath

parts.text: David reaches Nob and tells Ahimelech the priest that he is on a confidential royal mission. Lacking ordinary bread, the priest gives him the shewbread removed from before the LORD, after discussing the men’s ceremonial condition. David also receives Goliath’s sword. Doeg the Edomite, one of Saul’s servants, is present and sees him there.

David flees to Achish king of Gath, but the king’s servants recognize him and recall the songs celebrating his victories. Afraid of what this recognition may bring, David pretends to be mad, making marks on the gate and letting saliva run down his beard. Achish dismisses him as a madman and objects to his being brought into the household.

chapters.title: Saul destroys the priests of Nob

parts.text: David gathers his family and about four hundred distressed, indebted, or discontented men at Adullam. He places his parents under Moab’s protection, then follows Gad’s direction to return to Judah. Meanwhile Saul accuses his servants of conspiring with David. Doeg reports seeing Ahimelech give David food and Goliath’s sword and inquire of the LORD for him.

Saul summons the priestly household and accuses Ahimelech of conspiracy. Ahimelech defends David’s reputation and denies knowing any rebellion. Saul orders the priests killed, but his guards refuse. Doeg kills eighty-five priests and devastates Nob, including its families and animals. Abiathar escapes to David, who acknowledges that he knew Doeg would report him to Saul and accepts responsibility for the deaths. He promises Abiathar protection.

chapters.title: David rescues Keilah and evades Saul

parts.text: David hears that Philistines are raiding Keilah and twice seeks the LORD’s direction. God assures him of victory, and he rescues the town. Saul plans to trap him there, but David inquires through the ephod brought by Abiathar and learns that Keilah’s men would surrender him. David and his six hundred men leave. Saul searches continually, but God does not deliver David into his hand.

Jonathan visits David in the wilderness and strengthens his trust in God, affirming that David will become king. The Ziphites reveal David’s whereabouts to Saul. Pursuit brings Saul close to surrounding him near Maon, but news of a Philistine invasion forces Saul to withdraw. David then moves to the strongholds of En-gedi.

chapters.title: David spares Saul in the cave

parts.text: Saul takes three thousand chosen men to search for David at En-gedi. He enters a cave where David and his men are hiding. David’s followers see an opportunity for killing the king, but David only cuts off part of Saul’s robe. Even this troubles his conscience, and he restrains his men, refusing to lay a hand on the LORD’s anointed.

After Saul leaves, David calls after him and displays the cut piece as proof that he could have killed him but chose mercy. He appeals to the LORD to judge between them. Saul weeps, admits David’s righteousness, and acknowledges that David will become king. He asks protection for his descendants, which David swears to provide. Saul returns home, while David remains in the stronghold.

chapters.title: Abigail prevents bloodshed

parts.text: Samuel dies and Israel mourns. David asks the wealthy Nabal for provisions during sheep-shearing, reminding him that his shepherds were protected by David’s men. Nabal insults the request and refuses. David arms his men and vows destruction against Nabal’s household. A servant warns Abigail, Nabal’s wise wife, who quickly gathers food and goes to meet David without telling her husband.

Abigail humbly takes responsibility, urges David to leave vengeance to the LORD, and warns against needless bloodshed that would later burden him as ruler. David blesses God for sending her and abandons his revenge. After Abigail tells Nabal, he becomes as a stone; about ten days later the LORD strikes him, and he dies. David then marries Abigail. The chapter also names Ahinoam as his wife and notes Saul’s giving Michal to another man.

chapters.title: David again spares Saul

parts.text: The Ziphites report David’s location, and Saul again pursues him with three thousand men. David and Abishai enter Saul’s camp by night while a deep sleep from the LORD rests on the army. Abishai offers to kill Saul with his spear, but David refuses to strike the LORD’s anointed. They take the spear and water cruse beside Saul’s head and withdraw.

From a safe distance, David rebukes Abner for failing to guard the king and asks Saul why he pursues an innocent servant. Saul confesses folly and promises harm no longer. David returns the spear and entrusts his life to the LORD, who rewards righteousness and faithfulness. Saul blesses him and predicts his success, but the two men go separate ways.

chapters.title: David lives under Achish at Ziklag

parts.text: Fearing that Saul will eventually destroy him, David takes his six hundred men and their households into Philistine territory under Achish of Gath. Saul stops pursuing him. David asks for a country town rather than residence in the royal city, and Achish gives him Ziklag. The chapter records his stay in Philistine territory as a year and four months.

David raids the Geshurites, Gezrites, and Amalekites, taking livestock and clothing and leaving no survivors to report his actions. He tells Achish that his raids target districts associated with Judah and its allies. Achish therefore believes David has made himself hateful to Israel and will remain permanently in his service, unaware of the true targets.

chapters.title: Saul consults the woman at En-dor

parts.text: As the Philistines prepare for war, Achish expects David to accompany him. Saul sees the enemy army and is afraid. The LORD does not answer him by dreams, Urim, or prophets. Although Saul had expelled those with familiar spirits, he disguises himself and visits a woman at En-dor, asking her to bring up Samuel. She fears punishment, then recognizes Saul during the encounter.

Samuel rebukes Saul for disturbing him and declares that the LORD has become his enemy because of his disobedience concerning Amalek. The kingdom has been given to David, and Israel will be defeated; Saul and his sons will be with Samuel the next day. Saul collapses in fear and weakness. The woman and his servants persuade him to eat before leaving that night.

chapters.title: The Philistine rulers send David away

parts.text: As the Philistine forces assemble, their rulers object to David and his men marching with Achish. Achish defends David as a faithful servant, but the commanders fear that he could regain Saul’s favour by turning against them in battle. They recall the song crediting him with killing tens of thousands and insist that he return to the place assigned to him.

Achish tells David that he personally finds no fault in him but must yield to the other rulers. David protests his exclusion from fighting, yet Achish repeats the order to leave early in the morning. David and his men return toward Philistine territory, while the Philistine army advances toward Jezreel.

chapters.title: David recovers the captives taken from Ziklag

parts.text: David returns to find Ziklag burned and all the families taken captive by Amalekites. His men grieve bitterly and speak of stoning him, but he strengthens himself in the LORD. Through Abiathar he seeks God’s direction and receives assurance of recovery. Two hundred exhausted men remain behind while four hundred pursue. They revive an abandoned Egyptian servant, who agrees to guide them to the raiders.

David attacks the Amalekites and recovers every captive and possession, including his wives. Some men oppose sharing the spoil with those who stayed behind, but David declares that those guarding the baggage must share equally with the fighters, establishing a rule. He also sends gifts from the spoil to elders in Judah’s towns where he and his men had stayed.

chapters.title: Saul and his sons die in battle

parts.text: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa and kill Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua. Badly wounded by archers, Saul asks his armourbearer to kill him rather than let the Philistines abuse him. When the man refuses, Saul falls on his own sword, and the armourbearer does likewise. Israelites abandon nearby towns, which the Philistines occupy.

Finding the bodies, the Philistines cut off Saul’s head, take his armour, and display his body on Beth-shan’s wall, announcing victory in their idol temples. The valiant men of Jabesh-gilead travel through the night, recover Saul’s body and those of his sons, and bring them home. They burn the bodies, bury the bones under a tree, and fast seven days.
